topic: Calculating grocery spending from a budget percentage
core_question: A household budget of $1,800 allocates 25% to groceries. How much is spent on groceries?

messages.content: So we're doing budget percentages. A household budget is 1800 and 25 percent goes to groceries. How much is that?
When you hear '25 percent of 1800,' what operation comes to mind?
Ugh, just give me the number. I'm starving and this is taking forever.
I get it—but wouldn't it be faster if you grabbed the calculation yourself instead of waiting for me to tell you?
One word. That's all I'm asking.
Is a one-word answer actually going to help you on a test where you have to show your thinking?
Okay, whatever. So if it's 25 percent, I divide or multiply?
What does a percentage usually mean—is it a part of the whole, or is it something added on top?
It's part of the whole. So I multiply 0.25 times 1800?
Does that feel right based on what you just said about it being a part of the whole?
Yeah, that makes sense. I can do that.
Do you feel ready to handle this kind of problem on your own next time?
